transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Aria Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (Catalyst DS), Tom Reynolds (Catalyst ML Infra), Eva Martinez (Catalyst CTO), Samir Kaur (Catalyst Security)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — last week's INT8 run results, FP8 exploratory run, quality checks, next steps.
[00:18] Priya: Yep, thanks Maya. We ran the INT8 profile on 4 nodes overnight, saw lower latency but some weird token-level diffs on a small subset.
[00:30] Liam: Right, the aggregate numbers look good — p50 dropped from 80ms to ~62ms on our shorter prompts, throughput up ~18-22% depending on batch sizing. But there are a few tail cases where generation changes a bit.
[00:45] Tom: Can you clarify "token-level diffs" — is that hallucination-y or just phrasing?
[00:52] Aria: Mostly phrasing, a handful of examples where the model picks a synonym or drops a small clause; one case looked like a mild factual flip. We flagged those in the eval set.
[01:10] Eva: How bad is the factual flip? Business impact?
[01:16] Priya: One medical summary mis-ordered the sequence of events; it's a low percent but not zero. That's why we're cautious.
[01:25] Maya: Important flag. INT8 is giving us cost and perf wins but we need to tune the calibration and maybe preserve higher precision for specific layers or heads.
[01:40] Liam: We tried per-layer mixed precision heuristics — keeping output projection at FP16 while quantizing others to INT8 reduced the regression rate by ~60% in our sample.
[01:55] Tom: Did you use, uh, symmetric or asymmetric quantization?
[02:02] Liam: Asymmetric on activations, symmetric on weights, and we did a small calibration dataset — about 5k tokens sampled from prod-like prompts. Might need broader sampling.
[02:18] Priya: We can expand the calibration set; I can push another 20k prompts that include edge-case medical wording.
[02:25] Maya: Great.
[02:30] [02:30] Maya: FP8 notes — Oliver ran an FP8 exploratory run over the weekend; Oliver, can you summarize?
[02:38] Oliver: Sure. FP8 pushed throughput further — p50 down to ~55ms on the same prompt mix and throughput +30% vs baseline. But quality regressions were slightly higher than INT8 for this model family, especially on rare entity handling. There were also more numerical instabilities on long-context cases.
[03:05] Samir: From security standpoint, any change in deterministic outputs matters for audit logs — we need to capture drift.
[03:12] Maya: Yeah we'll include a regression tracking bucket.
[03:17] [03:17] Priya: Did you observe KV cache interaction issues? We sometimes see state mismatch after quantization.
[03:24] Liam: Good call. There were a couple cache pointer misses where chunking boundary leads to off-by-one logits — mostly due to tokenization differences + lower precision accumulation. We're working on stable accumulation (higher precision for KV accumulation) which cuts those cases dramatically.
[03:45] Tom: So recommended config is INT8 with FP16 accumulation on KV?
[03:50] Aria: For now yes, for the POC that's the conservative approach. For FP8 we'd need FP16 accumulation and additional stochastic rounding to be safe.
[04:05] [04:05] Priya: Can you share the raw diffs? We want to triage by severity (cosmetic vs business-critical).
[04:11] Liam: Already uploaded a short CSV and a folder with raw samples to the shared drive (link in the chat). We'll push the full perf CSV by EOD.
[04:22] [04:22] Priya: Cool. On cost: what's the unit cost delta if we go full INT8 vs baseline FP16?
[04:29] Maya: Ballpark — for your workload we'd expect ~22-28% cost savings at the token level after accounting for batching and KV cache hit rates. FP8 could be up to ~35% but with more risk. We'll put together a pricing delta sheet.
[04:45] Eva: For production we need SLA and rollback plan. If we see a regression we need canary and auto-fallback to FP16.
[04:54] Maya: Agreed. Redwood supports route-based fallback and model variant routing. We can stage a canary for 5% traffic and automatic rollback on quality regression thresholds.
[05:10] Tom: What's the plan for calibration sets and continuous monitoring?
[05:15] Aria: Proposal: expand calibration to 25k prompts including high-risk medical phrasing, run 48h stability with traffic replay on staging, collect BLEU/ROUGE-ish and task-specific metrics plus human spot checks.
[05:30] Priya: Human spot checks — we can do a 50-sample monthly review + automated alerts on divergence metrics.
[05:37] [05:37] Samir: Security question: KMS integration — if we use Redwood private KMS/HSM, what are the steps? Any extra latency?
[05:46] Maya: We'll send KMS integration doc. Latency is negligible for inference; key ops are at model load time not per-request. For private deployments we support customer-managed keys.
[06:00] Priya: Also need audit logs and token-level cost breakdown for compliance.
[06:05] Oliver: Console already provides token-level cost and per-route dashboards; we'll export a sample report.
[06:12] [06:12] Tom: Quick nit — in the FP8 run you mentioned "numerical instability" on long contexts; could you show an example?
[06:20] Liam: Sure, one example where the model repeats a clause after 2.5k tokens. We suspect accumulation rounding. We'll attach examples.
[06:30] Priya: Ok. If we do INT8 with selective FP16 layers, what's the expected perf delta?
[06:36] Liam: Expect a compromise: p50 ~60-65ms, throughput ~+20%, and regression rate drops to near INT8-best-effort — our small tests show about ~5% of the previous regressions remain.
[06:52] [06:52] Maya: Let's clarify acceptance criteria for the POC. Eva, Tom?
[06:57] Eva: Business acceptance: less than 0.5% high-severity regressions on our clinical eval set and at least 15% reduction in token cost.
[07:08] Tom: And infra acceptance: stable KV cache behavior over 48h with <1 incident and no memory leaks.
[07:15] Maya: Great. We'll aim for those thresholds.
[07:20] [07:20] Priya: Any blockers?
[07:23] Samir: Need SOC2 docs and KMS notes.
[07:26] Maya: We'll send security pack and a short KMS/HSM integration checklist.
[07:32] [07:32] Maya: Next steps recap: Redwood to share full perf CSV and raw samples (Liam), send SOC2/KMS notes (Maya), customer runs 48h staging test (Tom), and we'll reconvene after results.
[07:48] Eva: Sounds good. Also please include competitor notes — we're evaluating OpenAI/Anthropic too, want side-by-side numbers.
[07:55] Maya: We'll add a comparison row; note different model families so it's approximate.
[08:02] [08:02] Priya: One more question on rollout: if canary triggers fallback, how fast can you route back?
[08:09] Maya: We can route on metrics in near real-time (couple minutes) and we have automatic fallback policies.
[08:15] Tom: Ok let's target the 48h run starting Monday and follow-up next Thursday same time.
[08:22] Maya: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[08:26] [08:26] End of transcript.
